notes:
Core Run, Satin and Tatami routing improvements.

- Section underlay is placed before the finished cover it crosses, including crossings introduced by machine-file rounding.
- Generated travel is checked against stitches sewn later. Unverified exposed travel uses a needle-up transfer instead of sewing over a finished surface.
- Fewer unnecessary Tatami transfers around cutouts. One default square-hole control improves from 74 to 5 jumps; a difficult Double Zigzag control improves from 96 to 52 jumps while correcting its support order.
- Underlay changes retain the tested cover paths, including reversed fills, curved cutouts and narrow multi-hole shapes. Connector locks use the final routing.
- Run improvements cover closed seams, interior exits, hand-stitch routing and Zigzag approaches. Satin improvements cover cutout turns, shortening and sectional support anchors.
- Auto Digitize uses the same updated engine. Installer and portable editions use the same update channel.

Offline qualification includes 246 native tests, 301 underlay profiles at 25 export-grid offsets, closest joins, EXP export, startup and rendering. Additional integration results are retained in the progress checklist.

Known limitations: full parity is not complete. Complex fills can still have excess jumps/trims; the default minimum-transfer control has 5 jumps against a target of 1. Some Satin corner short moves and unequal A/B Run spacing remain under review. Trimming-disabled machines can leave connecting threads. Physical sew-out validation is deferred. Review the stitch sequence before sewing.
